descriptionChirho: The act of rising from the dead, specifically the eschatological or Christological resurrection — the raising of the dead to new life. This is the dominant NT theological sense (41 of 42 occurrences). Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'resurrección,' Hindi 'पुनरुत्थान' (punarutthān = re-rising), Arabic 'قِيَامَةِ/القِيامَةِ' (qiyāma, the standard Islamic-Christian term for resurrection), Korean '부활' (buhwal = resurrection), Swahili 'ufufuo' (from -fufua, to raise from death). Used of Christ's resurrection (Matt 22:23-31; Acts 1:22; Rom 6:5; Phil 3:10), the general resurrection (John 5:29; 11:24-25), and the resurrection of the righteous (Luke 14:14; 20:35-36).

labelChirho: rising, rise (figurative, of destiny or restoration)
descriptionChirho: A figurative rising or uplifting — not resurrection from physical death but a metaphorical rise in status, destiny, or spiritual condition. Found in Luke 2:34 where Simeon prophesies that Jesus is set for the 'fall and rising' (πτῶσιν καὶ ἀνάστασιν) of many in Israel. Multilingual evidence distinguishes this from the resurrection sense: Spanish 'levantamiento' (uprising, rising — not 'resurrección'), Hindi 'उठने' (uṭhne = to rise/get up, not पुनरुत्थान), Arabic 'قِيَامِ' (qiyām = standing/rising, without the definite article القيامة of eschatological resurrection), Korean '일어남을 위하여' (ireonam = rising/getting up, not 부활), Swahili 'kufufuka' (to rise — verbal infinitive rather than the nominal 'ufufuo').
